name: BACK ALLEY
description: Back Alley is a robust partnership trick-taking game that originated in the American military. It combines the bidding intensity of Spades with the fluctuating hand sizes of Oh Hell!. Played with two unique Jokers known as 'Bloopers', the game follows a 26-hand schedule that tests a team's ability to communicate and predict trick counts under constantly changing conditions. Its reputation is built on high-pressure bidding where missing a contract results in severe point penalties.

content.text: Back Alley is a robust partnership trick-taking game that originated in the American military. It combines the bidding intensity of Spades with the fluctuating hand sizes of Oh Hell!. Played with two unique Jokers known as 'Bloopers', the game follows a 26-hand schedule that tests a team's ability to communicate and predict trick counts under constantly changing conditions. Its reputation is built on high-pressure bidding where missing a contract results in severe point penalties.

Back Alley, also called Back Alley Bridge or Back Street Bridge, originated in the American military, probably during World War II. It grew out of servicemen’s barracks games and spread through off-base social circles as a high-intensity partnership trick-taking game.
4 players in North-South and East-West partnerships.
54 cards including Big Joker and Little Joker.
Standard deck, 2 distinct Jokers, score sheet.
Deal starts at 13 cards each. Subsequent hands decrease by 1 until the 1-card hand, then increase back to 13, for a full 26-deal 13‑1‑13 schedule.

items.text: Army Straight: Played without Jokers; the 2 of the trump suit is the highest card in the game.
Back Alley Bridge: Bidding is done by teams simultaneously using signals rather than in rotation.
